# Harrison

## Overview

- **Age:** middle-aged  <sub>[v2 c13 P7](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0007)</sub>
- **Gender:** male  <sub>[v2 c1 P4](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0004)</sub>
- **Origin:** Scottsford, New Brunswick  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>
- **Role:** farmer  <sub>[v2 c13 P7](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0007), [v2 c17 P8](../source/v02-c17.md#nw-v02-c17-p0008)</sub>
- **Titles:** Mr.  <sub>[v2 c1 P3](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0003)</sub>

## Appearance

Mr. Harrison is short, fat, and bald, with a round face and prominent blue eyes. When enraged, his face turns purple and his eyes protrude. After reconciling with his wife, he presents a much neater and more snug appearance.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P11](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0011), [v2 c28 P8](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0008)_

## Personality

Regarded locally as an odd crank, Mr. Harrison is fussy, fidgety, and notoriously outspoken. He prides himself on telling the truth no matter how plain it is, though he can be cantankerous and hard to please. Beneath his crusty exterior, he is sympathetic, kind, and capable of warm, sociable friendships.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c3 P25](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0025), [v2 c3 P39](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0039), [v2 c9 P40](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0040), [v2 c20 P8](../source/v02-c20.md#nw-v02-c20-p0008), [v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057), [v3 c12 P39](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0039)_

## History

After moving from New Brunswick to Avonlea in early April, Mr. Harrison lived as a bachelor on his farm, hiring young John Henry Carter to assist him. He quickly gained a reputation as an eccentric crank due to his irregular meals and his foul-mouthed parrot, Ginger. Shortly after his arrival, he angrily confronted Anne Shirley over a Jersey cow that had escaped into his grain, though the two quickly patched things up and became good friends. While keeping his past separation from his wife Emily a secret, he was rumored by local gossips to be courting Isabella Andrews when he merely visited her home to play checkers with Harmon Andrews. Eventually, his wife Emily relocated to Avonlea to reunite with him following the death of Ginger, after which Mr. Harrison transformed his habits, attending church regularly and dressing neatly. He maintained a close friendship with Anne, offering honest, blunt feedback on her early writing efforts before she left for college.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P3](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0003), [v2 c1 P4](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0004), [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c1 P6](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0006), [v2 c1 P10](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0010), [v2 c3 P39](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0039), [v2 c24 P5](../source/v02-c24.md#nw-v02-c24-p0005), [v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057), [v2 c25 P59](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0059), [v2 c28 P8](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0008), [v3 c11 P50](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0050), [v3 c12 P39](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0039), [v3 c12 P41](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0041)_

## Background by volume

- visited Prince Edward Island as a boy  <sub>[v2 c25 P59](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0059)</sub>
- lived in Scottsford, New Brunswick, kept by his sister until her death  <sub>[v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>
- promised his dying sister he would marry Emily Scott  <sub>[v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>
- took a fortnight's wedding trip to St. John  <sub>[v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>
- separated from his wife after constant bickering over housecleaning and his profane parrot Ginger  <sub>[v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>
- bought Robert Bell's farm in Avonlea in early April  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>

## Quotes

> But you mustn’t mind me, I’m a terrible outspoken old fellow, that’s all . . . awful apt to tell the truth, no matter if it is a bit plain.  <sub>[v2 c3 P25](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0025)</sub>

> That old nuisance of a Rachel Lynde was here again today, pestering me for a subscription towards buying a carpet for the vestry room. I detest that woman more than anybody I know. She can put a whole sermon, text, comment, and application, into six words, and throw it at you like a brick.  <sub>[v2 c9 P0](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0000)</sub>

> But your folks ain’t like real folks anywhere. They talk too much and use too high-flown language. There’s one place where that Dalrymple chap talks even on for two pages, and never lets the girl get a word in edgewise. If he’d done that in real life she’d have pitched him.  <sub>[v3 c12 P45](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0045)</sub>
